youtube.title: The CIA Tried to Turn a Cat Into a Spy | Acoustic Kitty
youtube.description:
In the 1960s, the CIA's Acoustic Kitty project fitted a cat with a microphone in its ear canal, a transmitter at the base of its skull and an antenna woven through its fur, hoping it could eavesdrop near targets. By one estimate it cost about $20 million. A famous account says the first cat was hit by a taxi on its first test; that story is disputed. The project was abandoned in 1967. Documents were released in 2001 after a FOIA request by the National Security Archive.

📂 Case File #019: Acoustic Kitty

Sources: Smithsonian Magazine, "The CIA Experimented on Animals in the 1960s, Too. Just Ask 'Acoustic Kitty'"; Mental Floss, "The CIA Plan to Use Cats as Spies (and the Taxi That Ruined It)".
Images (Wikimedia Commons): CIA floor seal and Original Headquarters rendering (public domain); cats by Basile Morin (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Tadeáš Bednarz (CC BY-SA 4.0).
